epistemic_summary.statement: 0 of the 2,000 catalogued problems in the Unsolved Problems Mega-Atlas are solved by this work. Two entries answer a question that another author stated as open in an arXiv preprint: Conjecture 7.7 of Banić and Elezović (arXiv:2610.17046v1) in 0TH-2026-006, and the limit question of Section 6 of Muller and Saniga (arXiv:2609.19862v1) in 0TH-2026-009 Track 2, where the identification of the formal objects with the preprint's hypergraphs rests partly on argument outside Lean. 0TH-2026-009 Track 1 also proves strict-law failure for one representative of each case of Jonah's Conjecture E from an unreviewed Zenodo preprint, with Theorem B4 cited from outside Lean. Neither these sources nor these proofs are peer reviewed. Each row's class follows the strongest kind among its results in RESULTS.md. Of the other 26 rows, 4 are new-theorem suites, 2 bounded or partial cases, 7 formalizations of known results (1 of them a barrier formalization) and 13 invariant suites of software models. Entries without a machine-checked result at their pinned commit have no row; RESULTS.md lists them with the reason.

entries.target_statement: Exact minimum Kochen-Specker set sizes inside finite coordinate pools. Lean 4.35.0 (zero Mathlib, six kernels in CI) proves 31 for the 49 rays of B(3,2) (integer entries |c| <= 2) and 18 for the 40 rays of {0,+1,-1}^4. SAT/DRUP certificates, checked by the project's own checker, support 31 for |c| <= 3 and |c| <= 4, 33 for 3D rays with entries 0 or N-th roots of unity (N = 6, 12, 18, 24), and 29 for {0,+1,-1}^5.

entries.target_statement: Track 2 answers the stacking-limit question of Muller & Saniga (arXiv:2609.19862v1, Sec. 6; unreviewed preprint) for k disjoint Peres-Mermin squares and k Mermin pentagrams: exact degrees (7^k - 5^k)/2 and (6^k - 4^k)/2 with genuine assignment minimum actualMinViolations so epsilon_k -> 1, literal 2- and 3-qubit Pauli realizations, 4- and 6-qubit bridges, kernel-decided equality with HS(L(K_{3,3})) and HS(Petersen), and arbitrary-k Support.lean instantiation (SeedSupport.lean). Track 1 proves, for every N >= 4, formal geometric vertex-case membership (IsCaseC1-IsCaseC15, ConjectureECases.lean) and strict-law failure for one representative of each of the nine vertex cases of Jonah's Conjecture E (unreviewed Zenodo preprint; C1 and C6 were already proved there; coverage of whole cases uses Jonah's Theorem B4 outside Lean), exact binary completion optima 368 and 344 for one four-qubit C3 sign pair, and an infinite family of non-closed 3m-qubit Pauli sets attaining the spectral floor (contextual for m >= 2). Track 3 formalizes a finite-tree hitting bound z/T and the Peres-Mermin setting-bias floor min_c p(c).
